events.text: Before you move, you learn more about {npc} than the commission said: {he} has been paying for the medicine of an isle's whole hamlet, out of {his} own stones.

effects.log: You put the thought away. The work is the work.

choices.text: Spare them and tell the Pavilion nothing

effects.log: You let {npc} live. The Pavilion will learn it.
The client was the one who should have paid for the medicine. You go to them instead.

events.text: {npc} drinks only cloud-tea brewed by a single servant, and the servant takes the leaves from the same jar every dawn.

ok.log: The tea is strong that morning. {npc} does not finish it.

fail.log: The servant tastes it first and falls ill. The wardens come.

ok.log: The servant brews it. You never ask how they sleep.

fail.log: The servant runs to {npc}.

choices.text: Walk away before it is done

effects.log: You leave the jar untouched and go.

events.text: {npc} crosses the cloud road to the next isle every tenth day, by skiff, with four guards. The road narrows where the mist is thickest.

ok.log: The arrow comes out of the mist and {npc} goes into it.

fail.log: The guards close round {npc} and come for you.

ok.log: It is over before the guards turn round.

fail.log: The guards are better than you were told.

effects.log: You let it go into the mist.

events.text: You spend months as a lamp-tender in the pavilion of {npc}, under a borrowed name. Tonight {he} is alone, reading, and asks you to trim the wick.

ok.log: One touch at the neck. {npc} sleeps, and does not wake.

fail.log: {npc} turns at the last moment and shouts.

choices.text: Trim the wick, and leave in the morning

effects.log: You trim it, and go. You cannot say why.

events.text: You knock at the gate of {npc}'s pavilion and give your name, as the Pavilion's old law allows a challenger. {npc} comes out with a sword.

ok.log: It ends in one exchange above the clouds that nobody else sees.

fail.log: You are slower than you thought. {npc} lets you go, which is worse.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the name on a commission

effects.log: You bow. {npc} bows back. Neither of you will forget it.

events.text: The captain of {npc}'s guard is between you and the door: an immortal with a spear and no fear of you at all.

ok.log: The captain goes down, alive but finished, and the door opens.

fail.log: The captain is everything they say. You get away over the roof with the commission undone.
fail.deathCause: the captain of the guard on a commission

ok.log: You drop through the roof behind them.

fail.log: The roof is warded.

effects.log: You are gone into the clouds.

events.text: {npc} has found you on a bridge of the Isle Bazaar: grown, trained, with the face of the one you killed for the Pavilion long ago.

ok.log: You win. The feud ends on the bridge.

fail.log: You lose, and they do not finish it.

choices.text: Beat them and let them go

ok.log: You beat them and walk away.

fail.log: They are better than you thought.

ok.log: You talk until dawn. It is not forgiveness. It is something.

fail.log: They will not hear you.

effects.log: You leave. They will find you again.

events.text: A warrant hunter has your shape from a failed commission, and is asking at every mooring of the isle.

ok.log: They give up and fly on.

fail.log: They come close, and go, and will be back.

effects.log: You send them three isles away.

events.text: The Pavilion's lord sends for you, which happens to few: a cup of cloud-wine in a room with no windows, and a question about what you mean to be.

effects.log: The lord nods. You are trusted with more.
The lord smiles. That is the right answer, and dangerous.

events.text: Before the dream, you read the page of {npc} in the Book: {he} has been feeding a dying world with {his} own divinity for an age.

effects.log: You close the Book. The work is the work.
You leave the dream. The Hall will learn it.
The client was the god starving that world. You go to them.

events.text: {npc} drinks nectar from a single cup, filled every dawn by an attendant of clay.

choices.text: Pour a forgetting into the cup

ok.log: The nectar is sweet that dawn. {npc} forgets to be a god.

fail.log: The clay attendant tastes it and shatters. The Court hears.

choices.text: Reshape the attendant to do it

ok.log: It is done by a servant that cannot be judged.

fail.log: The clay remembers its maker and refuses.

effects.log: You leave it.

events.text: {npc} rides a procession of faith between two temples every age, and the road passes the dark side of the sun.

ok.log: The procession arrives without its god.

fail.log: The procession's guardians turn on you.

effects.log: You let it pass.

events.text: An age as a keeper in {npc}'s temple, under another name. Tonight {he} sleeps in the inner hall, and dreams.

ok.log: Inside the dream, it is gentle. {npc} does not wake.

fail.log: {npc} wakes inside the dream and calls the guard.

choices.text: Keep the temple one more night, and go

effects.log: You leave. You cannot say why.

events.text: You come to {npc}'s domain openly and say your name, as the Silent Hall's oldest rule allows. {npc} meets you at the border.

ok.log: It is a fair fight between gods, and you win it.

fail.log: You lose, and {npc} lets you go, which is worse.
fail.deathCause: a duel between gods for the Silent Hall

effects.log: You bow. {npc} remembers.

events.text: A god of watchfulness stands at the door of {npc}'s dream, awake, as such gods always are.

ok.log: The watcher falls asleep at last, and the dream is open.

fail.log: The watcher holds, and you wake bleeding light.
fail.deathCause: a god of watchfulness at the door of a dream

ok.log: You come in by a dream next door.

fail.log: They see you.

effects.log: You wake, far away.

events.text: {npc}, grown into a god, has found you at the Divine Exchange: the child of the god you ended for the Silent Hall.

ok.log: The feud ends there.

fail.log: You lose. They do not finish it.

choices.text: Beat them and let them go

ok.log: You beat them and leave.

fail.log: They are stronger now.

ok.log: You talk for an age. It will do instead of forgiveness.

fail.log: They will not hear you.

effects.log: You leave. Feuds among gods are patient.

events.text: A clerk of the Court is reading your page with a finger on a failed piece of quiet work.

ok.log: The clerk turns the page.

fail.log: The finger stays.

choices.text: Give them another page to read

effects.log: You give them a scandal of someone else.

events.text: The lord of the Silent Hall meets you in a dream of an empty hall, and asks what a god is for.

choices.text: Say: to end what should end

effects.log: The lord nods. You are trusted with more.

choices.text: Say: you do not know yet

effects.log: The lord laughs. Good.

events.text: Before you move, you learn more about {npc} than the paper said: {he} has been quietly feeding the poor of {his} town every winter.

effects.log: The Lodge keeps no list. You keep going.
You let {npc} live. The Lodge will learn it.
The one who paid was starving the town. You go to them.

events.text: {npc} keeps a cook who drinks and a taster who sleeps, and the wine comes in by the back door at dusk.

ok.log: {npc} goes to bed with a headache and does not get up.

fail.log: The taster is awake. You run, with a cudgel across your back.

ok.log: The cook does it. You never ask how they sleep.

fail.log: The cook runs to {npc}.

effects.log: You walk away.

events.text: {npc} rides the hill road with four guards on market days. The road narrows at the old bridge.

ok.log: It is over at the bridge.

fail.log: The guards come for you.

effects.log: You let them pass.

events.text: Months as a servant in the house of {npc}, under another name. Tonight {he} asks you to bring the lamp.

ok.log: One touch. {npc} sleeps, and does not wake.

fail.log: {npc} shouts.

choices.text: Bring the lamp and leave in the morning

effects.log: You go.

events.text: You knock on the gate of {npc} and give your name. {npc} comes out armed.

ok.log: A fair fight, and yours.

fail.log: A fair fight, and theirs. {npc} lets you crawl away.
fail.deathCause: a night duel for the Lodge

effects.log: You bow and go.

events.text: The captain of {npc}'s guard stands in the corridor between you and the door.

ok.log: The captain goes down, and the door opens.

fail.log: The captain holds. You get away over the wall.
fail.deathCause: the captain of the guard of a target

ok.log: You drop in behind.

fail.log: Tiles give way.

effects.log: You are gone.

events.text: {npc} has found you in the market square: grown, armed, with the face of the one you killed for the Lodge.

ok.log: The feud ends.

fail.log: You lose, and live.

choices.text: Beat them and let them go

ok.log: You walk away.

fail.log: They are better than you thought.

ok.log: It is not forgiveness, but it will do.

fail.log: They will not hear.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: Your face is on a notice at the town gate, badly drawn but not badly enough.

ok.log: A newer notice covers yours.

fail.log: People are still looking.

effects.log: They search the wrong hills.

events.text: The master of the Lampless Lodge meets you in a cellar with no lamp, and asks what you mean to become.

effects.log: You are trusted with more.
The master laughs, quietly.

events.text: The commission names {npc}. You watch {him} for a month first, as you always do, and learn that {he} once carried a stranger's child down the white stairs to a healer, and never told anyone.

effects.log: The Pavilion does not pay for what you learn. It pays for the work.

choices.text: Spare {him}, and lie to the Pavilion

effects.log: You report the target fled to another isle. The Pavilion will learn the truth one day.

choices.text: Follow the stones back to whoever paid

effects.log: The stones lead to a minister who would rather not repay what {npc} lent. You call on the minister instead.

events.text: {npc} keeps a garden of cloud-peaches and eats one every morning from the same tree, which {he} prunes with {his} own hands.

choices.text: Graft a poisoned branch onto the tree

ok.log: The tree bears one strange peach. {npc} eats it at dawn and lies down under the branches.

fail.log: The tree rejects the graft, loudly, and the garden's wards wake.

choices.text: Pay the gardener to choose the peach

ok.log: The gardener chooses. {npc} never asks why that one.

fail.log: The gardener keeps your stones and loves {npc} more.

choices.text: Leave the garden as it is

effects.log: You leave the peaches to ripen.

events.text: {npc} meditates every new moon on a pillar of rock that floats alone above the sea of cloud. Only one updraught reaches it.

choices.text: Ride the updraught in the dark

ok.log: You land behind {npc} without a sound, and the meditation does not end; it only stops.

fail.log: The updraught carries you in too fast. {npc} opens {his} eyes.

choices.text: Loose an arrow across the gap

ok.log: The arrow crosses the moonless gap. {npc} does not move again.

fail.log: The arrow is turned by a ward, and the alarm stone rings.

effects.log: You watch the pillar until dawn, and go home.

events.text: Under a borrowed name you have kept the scrolls of {npc} for a year. Tonight {he} asks you to read aloud to {him} until {he} falls asleep.

ok.log: You read to the end of the chapter. {npc} sleeps, and you close the book on {him}.

fail.log: {npc} is still awake at the end of the chapter, watching you.

choices.text: Read until {he} sleeps, and leave the scroll open

effects.log: In the morning the scroll-keeper is gone. {npc} wonders for a while, and hires another.

events.text: {npc} has heard that the Pavilion took a commission on {him}, and has sent you an invitation: the duelling terrace at noon, witnesses welcome.

choices.text: Go to the terrace at noon

ok.log: The witnesses go home with a story. {npc} does not go home.

fail.log: {npc} beats you in front of every witness on the isle, and lets you live to tell it.
fail.deathCause: a duel at noon on the name of a commission

effects.log: You do not go. The terrace waits all afternoon; the isles talk all season.

events.text: Between you and {npc} stand two war-puppets of starsteel, bought from a master and set to wake at any step they do not know.

ok.log: Starsteel rings on the floor. The door behind them is open.

fail.log: The puppets do not tire. You leave by the window with nothing done.
fail.deathCause: two war-puppets on a commission

ok.log: You learn the step they were set to know, and walk past in it.

fail.log: You get the step wrong.

effects.log: You leave the puppets to guard an untroubled night.

events.text: An apprentice of the Lotus Halls, {npc}, asks you for a word at the Lantern Guild's gate. {He} was the student of an immortal on one of your old commissions.

ok.log: It is over at the gate. The feud ends there.

fail.log: {npc} learned more than medicine.

ok.log: You leave {him} on the gate steps, beaten and alive.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay beaten.

ok.log: {npc} listens, goes very still, and walks away to find the one who paid.

fail.log: {npc} does not care who paid.

effects.log: You walk on through the gate. {npc} follows at a distance.

events.text: Your face from a failed commission is on a jade warrant at the Lantern Guild, and the Guild pays well for faces.

choices.text: Go to a far isle for a season

ok.log: By spring a new face is on the warrant board.

fail.log: A Guild factor recognises you at the moorings.

choices.text: Pay the Guild to lose the warrant

effects.log: Stones change hands. The warrant is filed somewhere nobody looks.

events.text: The Pavilion's lord takes you to the top of its tower, where the names of every commission are carved, and asks which of them you would undo.

effects.log: The lord nods once. More names will come to you.
The lord looks at the name you chose for a long time. "Good," the lord says. "Remember it."

events.text: The Silent Hall names {npc}, a god of lost things. When you look into {his} domain you see what {he} does all age: {he} finds what mortals lose and leaves it where they will look.

effects.log: The Hall does not ask what a god does. It asks whether you will.
You tell the Hall the dream was closed to you. The Hall will learn otherwise.
The one who paid lost something of their own once, and {npc} gave it back to the wrong person. You call on them instead.

events.text: {npc} breathes the incense of {his} worlds every dawn, as gods do. The incense of one small world reaches {him} last of all.

choices.text: Mix a forgetting into that world's incense

ok.log: {npc} breathes it in at dawn and forgets, one thing after another, that {he} is a god.

fail.log: The priests of that world smell it first and pray against it.

choices.text: Persuade a priest of that world to do it

ok.log: The priest does it, for a promise you will keep.

fail.log: The priest loves {his} god.

effects.log: You let the small world pray as it always has.

events.text: {npc} crosses the river between the stars once an age to visit a mortal grave. {He} goes alone.

ok.log: You do it before {he} kneels. You do not stay to see the grave.

fail.log: The grave's guardian sees you first.

ok.log: The river between the stars carries {npc} away.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger on that river than anywhere.

effects.log: You let {him} go. Even you will not do it there.

events.text: For an age you have been one of {npc}'s clay attendants, shaped and named by {him}. Tonight {he} asks you to stand at the foot of {his} bed while {he} dreams.

ok.log: The dream is of a world {npc} made long ago. You end it there, quietly.

fail.log: {npc} knows the clay of {his} own making.

choices.text: Stand guard until dawn, and leave

effects.log: At dawn one attendant is missing. {npc} counts them twice.

events.text: {npc} has read your name in the Book beside {his} own and comes to meet you first, at the border of the domain of war, as gods do.

ok.log: The War Domain watches, and keeps the result.

fail.log: The War Domain watches you lose.
fail.deathCause: a duel of gods at the border of war

effects.log: You do not come. The Book records it, in small letters.

events.text: Three lesser gods sworn to {npc} keep the gate of {his} sleep, each awake in turn.

roll.foeName: a sworn god at the gate of sleep

ok.log: The sworn god falls asleep at last, and so do the others.

fail.log: The sworn god wakes the other two.
fail.deathCause: sworn gods at the gate of a sleep

choices.text: Wait for the change of watch

ok.log: Between one watch and the next there is a breath. You go through it.

fail.log: The watch changes early.

effects.log: You leave. They never knew you were there.

events.text: A young god of a vengeful river, {npc}, has been following your procession for three domains. {His} worlds once prayed to a god you ended for the Hall.

ok.log: The river runs quiet after. The feud ends.

fail.log: {npc} drowns your procession and lets you live.

ok.log: You send {him} back to {his} riverbed.

fail.log: The river does not stay beaten.

ok.log: You bless the worlds that prayed to the god you ended. {npc} watches, and lets the river rest.

fail.log: {npc} refuses the blessing for them.

effects.log: You turn aside. Rivers are patient.

events.text: A judge's clerk has found your hand in a dream that ended badly, and is comparing it to every page in the Book.

ok.log: You write differently for an age. The clerk compares and finds nothing.

fail.log: The clerk finds a page you missed.

choices.text: Give the clerk a better case

effects.log: You leave a greater crime of another god on the clerk's desk.

events.text: The lord of the Silent Hall shows you a room of sleeping gods who will never wake, every one the Hall's work, and asks which of them you envy.

effects.log: The lord nods. You are trusted with more.
The lord is quiet for a long time. Then: "So do I."

events.text: The paper names {npc}. You watch the house a week first, and see {him} every evening teaching the stable boy to read by lamplight.

effects.log: You fold the paper away. The Lodge pays for the work, not the letters.
You tell the Lodge the house was empty. The Lodge will find out.
The coins came from a cousin who wants the house. You visit the cousin instead.

events.text: {npc} takes honey from {his} own hives every morning, on bread, and keeps the hives behind a locked gate.

ok.log: The honey is darker that morning. {npc} goes back to bed and stays there.

fail.log: The bees find you before the honey does.

ok.log: The hive-keeper carries the jar in. You never ask whether they guessed.

fail.log: The hive-keeper runs to {npc} with your coins.

effects.log: You leave the hives to their humming.

events.text: {npc} walks to the river every evening to watch the boats, alone, along a path through tall reeds.

ok.log: The reeds close over the path again.

fail.log: A boatman on the river sees you and shouts.

ok.log: It is quick, and the boats sail on.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger than {he} looks.

effects.log: You let {him} have the evening.

events.text: All winter you have chopped wood for the house of {npc} under another name. Tonight {he} asks you in to warm your hands by the fire.

ok.log: The fire burns low. {npc} sleeps in the chair, and does not wake.

fail.log: {npc} sees the paper in your sleeve.

choices.text: Warm your hands, and leave in the morning

effects.log: The woodpile is full and the woodcutter gone. {npc} wonders for a day.

events.text: {npc} has heard there is a paper with {his} name, and waits for you in the empty market square at dawn, sword drawn.

ok.log: The market opens on an empty square and a story.

fail.log: The market opens on you, beaten, and {npc} walking home.
fail.deathCause: a dawn duel for the Lodge

effects.log: You leave {him} waiting until the stalls open.

events.text: {npc} keeps two great dogs that sleep across the door and wake at a breath.

ok.log: The dogs sleep on, unhurt, after a little help. The door opens.

fail.log: The dogs wake the house.
fail.deathCause: the guard dogs of a target

choices.text: Make friends with the dogs first

ok.log: A week of scraps, and they wag at you. The door is yours.

fail.log: The dogs are not for sale.

effects.log: You leave them sleeping across the door.

events.text: {npc} has found you at a village wedding: grown, armed, with the eyes of the one you killed for the Lodge.

ok.log: Behind the barn it ends. The music never stops.

fail.log: {npc} beats you behind the barn and goes back to the dancing.

ok.log: You leave {him} by the barn, beaten and alive.

fail.log: {npc} gets up again.

ok.log: You tell {him} everything. {npc} goes home without a word, and does not come back.

fail.log: {npc} does not want the truth.

effects.log: You leave the wedding early. {npc} watches you go.

events.text: A town crier is reading your description at the crossroads, and it is a good description.

choices.text: Grow a beard and change towns

ok.log: Nobody looks twice at the bearded stranger.

fail.log: The beard is not enough.

choices.text: Pay the crier to read it wrong

effects.log: The crier reads it wrong, loudly, all week.

events.text: The master of the Lampless Lodge walks with you through a town at night, past every house where the Lodge has worked, and asks which you remember.

effects.log: The master nods. You are trusted with more.
The master stops walking. "Then learn to," the master says.

events.text: The commission names {npc}. Every immortal on the isle says the same about {him}: {he} lends stones and never asks for them back.

effects.log: The Pavilion does not pay for gossip. You put it away.
You report that {npc} left for the far isles. The Pavilion will check.
The stones lead to a debtor who would rather owe a corpse. You call on the debtor.

events.text: {npc} is younger than the commission said, barely up the white stairs, and spends {his} evenings teaching ferrymen to read.

effects.log: Young or not, the name is on the slip.
You let the young immortal keep {his} evenings. The Pavilion will hear of it.
The one who paid was a rival of {npc}'s teacher. You go to the rival.

events.text: You learn that {npc} once refused the Pavilion a commission of {his} own, on a name {he} thought did not deserve it.

effects.log: The Pavilion remembers refusals. So, tonight, do you.
You refuse too. It seems only fair.
The one who paid is the name {npc} once spared. You call on that one instead.

events.text: {npc} keeps a pill cauldron burning day and night and tastes every batch.

ok.log: The batch comes out perfect, by every sign. {npc} tastes it and lies down beside the cauldron.

fail.log: The cauldron turns the poison black, and {npc} smells it.

ok.log: The cauldron-keeper does it, and flies to the far isles the same night.

fail.log: The cauldron-keeper loves the master more than stones.

effects.log: You leave the fire to its work.

events.text: {npc} drinks only dew gathered from one white lotus at dawn.

choices.text: Treat the lotus in the night

ok.log: The dew is heavy that morning. {npc} drinks it and sits down by the pool for good.

fail.log: The lotus wilts in an hour, and {npc} knows why.

effects.log: You leave the lotus to its dew.

events.text: {npc} gives a banquet for the Eight Houses, and you have a place among the servers.

ok.log: {npc} raises the cup to the Eight Houses and never sets it down.

fail.log: A taster of the Eight Houses smells the cup first.

effects.log: You pour the wine and leave with the empty jars.

events.text: {npc} flies a cloud-crane to the Jade Court each dawn, over the Gorge of Winds, where the crane must fly low.

ok.log: The crane comes home without its rider.

fail.log: The crane screams, and {npc}'s escort wheels toward you.

ok.log: It is over above the gorge.

fail.log: You miss the crane and catch only the wind.

effects.log: You watch the crane fly on.

events.text: {npc} hosts a moon-viewing on a pavilion roof each autumn, and sends the guards down to the stairs so the guests can talk.

ok.log: The guests are looking at the moon. Nobody is looking at {npc}.

fail.log: A guest sees you on the eaves and cries out.

ok.log: You raise a cup with {npc}, and the evening ends with one guest fewer.

fail.log: The steward does not know your face.

effects.log: You watch the moon from the next isle, and go home.

events.text: {npc} walks the white stairs alone once a year, down to a grave below the clouds. Halfway down the mist is thick.

ok.log: The mist keeps what happens there.

fail.log: {npc} hears your step and is ready.

effects.log: You let {him} pass. Even you will not do it on those stairs.

events.text: Under another name you have tended {npc}'s cranes for a season. Tonight {he} comes to the roost alone to feed them.

ok.log: {npc} sleeps among the cranes, and the cranes go on eating.

fail.log: The cranes shriek and the house wakes.

choices.text: Hand {him} the feed, and leave by morning

effects.log: In the morning the crane-keeper is gone.

events.text: A year as {npc}'s ink servant. Tonight {he} asks you to stay while {he} writes a letter to someone below the clouds.

choices.text: Wait until the letter is sealed

ok.log: {npc} sleeps over the letter. You send it on yourself, as {he} would have.

fail.log: {npc} looks up from the letter at the wrong moment.

choices.text: Seal the letter for {him} and go

effects.log: You seal it, and leave the house before dawn.

events.text: For a season you have carried {npc}'s parasol on the isle roads. Tonight a storm comes, and the road home is empty.

ok.log: The storm covers everything. The parasol is found in the morning, upside down on the road.

fail.log: {npc} turns in the rain and sees your hand move.

choices.text: Hold the parasol to the door, and leave

effects.log: You see {him} to the door and walk away into the storm.

events.text: {npc} meets you at the Thunder Gate, where duels are fought in the lightning, and bows first.

ok.log: The lightning takes the fight's end and keeps it.

fail.log: The lightning chooses {npc}. You crawl out of the Gate alive.
fail.deathCause: a duel at the Thunder Gate

effects.log: You bow and leave the Gate to the storm.

events.text: {npc} has waited on the Lantern Guild's bridge every night for a month. Tonight you come.

ok.log: One lantern goes out on the bridge, then the rest burn on.

fail.log: {npc} sends you back across the bridge, beaten, and lets you live.
fail.deathCause: a duel on the Lantern bridge

effects.log: You turn back. {npc} waits another night, then stops.

events.text: You find {npc} meditating on a sunken isle. {He} opens {his} eyes before you land. "The Pavilion," {he} says. "Come, then."

ok.log: The sunken isle is quiet again.

fail.log: {npc} closes {his} eyes again before you are out of sight.
fail.deathCause: a duel on a sunken isle

effects.log: You bow, and {npc} closes {his} eyes.

events.text: A sworn blade of {npc}'s house keeps the threshold with two swords, and does not sleep.

ok.log: The swords go still. The door is open.

fail.log: The sworn blade is everything they say. You leave over the wall.
fail.deathCause: a sworn blade on a commission

ok.log: You drop through the roof behind the threshold.

fail.log: The roof is warded.

effects.log: You go back into the clouds.

events.text: A ward of white jade rings {npc}'s pavilion. It sings at any step it does not know.

ok.log: You learn its song and walk through it humming.

fail.log: The ward sings out across the isle.

ok.log: You are through before the ward finishes its first note.

fail.log: The ward is faster.

effects.log: You leave it to its song.

events.text: Three of {npc}'s disciples keep watch on the pavilion roof in turns, and none has ever missed a turn.

ok.log: The eldest disciple will wake in the morning with a headache. {npc} will not wake.

fail.log: The eldest disciple holds the roof.
fail.deathCause: a disciple on a commission

choices.text: Wait for the change of watch

ok.log: Between one watch and the next, you are in.

fail.log: The watch changes early.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: {npc} has piloted your skiff for a month under another name. Halfway across the sea of cloud {he} lets go of the pole and turns: the face of one you ended for the Pavilion, younger.

ok.log: The skiff comes home with one aboard.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you remember being at that age.

ok.log: You leave {him} the skiff and fly home.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay down.

ok.log: You talk until the skiff drifts ashore. It is not forgiveness. It is a start.

fail.log: {npc} will not hear a word of it.

effects.log: You step off the skiff into the mist.

events.text: {npc} challenges you on the Duelling Terraces, in front of everyone, and names the immortal you ended for the Pavilion as {his} master.

ok.log: The terrace goes quiet. The feud ends there.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you remember being at that age.

ok.log: You leave {him} on the terrace, beaten, alive, and watched.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay down.

ok.log: You tell the terrace who paid. {npc} goes to find the one who paid.

fail.log: {npc} will not hear a word of it.

effects.log: You leave the terrace. The isles talk for a year.

events.text: The Pavilion's lord sends you a cloud-peach and a blank commission slip, with a note: "Write a name. Any name."

effects.log: The lord is pleased. You are trusted with more.
A second note comes: "Interesting." Nothing else, yet.

events.text: Your face from a failed commission is on a jade poster at every Lantern Guild counter, and the Guild sells copies.

choices.text: Buy every copy through other hands

ok.log: The poster disappears from the isles.

fail.log: The Guild prints more.

choices.text: Have another face drawn over yours

effects.log: A stranger's face goes up over yours, and the wardens chase it.

events.text: The Hall names {npc}, a god of thresholds. In {his} worlds no door is ever locked against a beggar.

effects.log: The Hall does not weigh doors. Neither will you.
You tell the Hall the dream would not open. It will learn otherwise.
The one who paid keeps locked doors. You call there instead.

events.text: {npc} gave away half {his} domain an age ago to a god who had lost theirs, and never asked for it back.

effects.log: An old kindness is not your business.
You leave {npc} the half {he} kept.
The one who paid is the god {npc} helped. You go to that god.

events.text: {npc} is a god of small hours, and the only one who answers prayers at night.

effects.log: Somebody else can answer at night.
You let the night keep its god.
The one who paid sells lamps. You visit the lamp-seller.

events.text: {npc} eats one star-peach from {his} own orchard each age, picked by {his} own hand.

choices.text: Ripen a forgetting in the peach

ok.log: {npc} eats it slowly, and forgets, one by one, every world {he} kept.

fail.log: The orchard's god-tree sheds the peach before it ripens.

effects.log: You leave the peaches to their age.

events.text: {npc} bathes in a river of the first light every dawn. The river comes from a spring nobody watches.

ok.log: The light is dim that dawn. {npc} goes into it and does not come out.

fail.log: The spring's spirit wakes and calls for the Court.

ok.log: The spirit does it, for a promise.

fail.log: The spirit loves its god.

effects.log: You let the river run clear.

events.text: At the Feast of Domains, {npc} drinks from a cup only {his} cupbearer may fill. You have been the cupbearer for an age.

ok.log: The feast goes on. One seat is empty by the end.

fail.log: An elder god at the next seat smells the cup.

choices.text: Fill it with nectar, and resign

effects.log: You fill it honestly and leave the feast for good.

events.text: {npc} crosses the bridge of stars between two domains alone, every hundred years, to count {his} worlds.

ok.log: The count stops at nine hundred and some.

fail.log: The bridge's guardians see the arrow first.

ok.log: The bridge is empty again.

fail.log: {npc} is strong on {his} own bridge.

effects.log: You let {him} count.

events.text: {npc} goes down to a mortal world each age, in disguise, to walk its market for a day.

ok.log: A stranger falls ill in the market, and the market goes on.

fail.log: {npc} sees through your disguise first.

effects.log: You leave the god to the stalls.

events.text: {npc} sleeps an age at a time in a cloud above {his} domain, and the cloud drifts with no guard.

ok.log: The cloud drifts on, lighter.

fail.log: The cloud is a guard after all.

effects.log: You watch it go.

events.text: For an age you have tended the lamps in {npc}'s temple. Tonight {he} comes to the inner hall alone to pray to {his} own maker.

ok.log: The prayer ends in silence, as all prayers do.

fail.log: {npc} hears you over the prayer.

effects.log: In the morning the lamp-keeper is gone.

events.text: You are one of {npc}'s heralds, and tonight {he} sends you with a message only you may hear the answer to.

ok.log: You deliver it in person.

fail.log: {npc} reads it in your face.

choices.text: Carry the message, and do not come back

effects.log: The message arrives. The herald does not return.

events.text: An age as {npc}'s gardener of stars. Tonight {he} walks the garden alone and asks you which star is ready.

ok.log: {npc} looks up at the star, and does not look down again.

fail.log: {npc} looks down at the wrong moment.

effects.log: You name one. In the morning the gardener is gone.

events.text: {npc} meets you at the border of the War Domain, where gods have always settled such things.

ok.log: The War Domain keeps the result.

fail.log: The War Domain watches you lose.
fail.deathCause: a duel of gods at the War Domain

effects.log: You bow. The War Domain is disappointed.

events.text: {npc} waits for you in the Hall of the Book, before the page with both your names.

ok.log: The Book closes one line.

fail.log: The Book writes your defeat in small letters.
fail.deathCause: a duel before the Book

effects.log: You leave the page as it is.

events.text: You come to {npc}'s throne openly. {He} stands, and the domain stands with {him}.

ok.log: The domain sits down again, under nobody.

fail.log: The domain throws you out across three borders.
fail.deathCause: a duel for a domain

effects.log: You bow to the throne and go.

events.text: Four lesser gods sworn to {npc} hold the four doors of {his} sleep.

choices.text: Go through the north door's god

roll.foeName: a sworn god of the north door

ok.log: The north door opens.

fail.log: The north door holds, and all four wake.
fail.deathCause: a sworn god at the door of a sleep

ok.log: There is always a fifth door. You find it.

fail.log: There is no fifth door.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: A beast of the Star Beast Stable lies across {npc}'s threshold, and it has never been asleep.

ok.log: The beast lies still, unhurt and asleep at last.

fail.log: The beast drives you off, roaring.
fail.deathCause: a star beast on the quiet work

ok.log: An age of patience, and it lets you pass.

fail.log: It will not be befriended.

effects.log: You leave the beast to its watch.

events.text: {npc} has set {his} own shadow to guard {him} while {he} dreams.

ok.log: The shadow lies down, and so does its god.

fail.log: The shadow is as strong as its god.
fail.deathCause: a god's shadow on the quiet work

ok.log: At noon a shadow is smallest. You step over it.

fail.log: Noon in that domain never comes.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: {npc}, the heir of a god you ended for the Hall, has taken {his} parent's domain and come to the border of yours.

ok.log: The border is quiet after.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you remember being at that age.

ok.log: You send {him} back to {his} domain.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay down.

ok.log: You give {him} the page of the Book that names who paid.

fail.log: {npc} will not hear a word of it.

effects.log: You withdraw from your border for an age.

events.text: A priest-god of the domain you emptied for the Hall, {npc}, has walked all the way to your temple to ask why.

ok.log: The question dies with {him}.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you remember being at that age.

ok.log: You send {him} home without an answer.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay down.

ok.log: You tell {him} why. {npc} walks home with it.

fail.log: {npc} will not hear a word of it.

effects.log: You close the temple doors.

events.text: The lord of the Silent Hall asks you to sit in on a judgement of the Court, unseen, and say afterwards who should have been sealed.

effects.log: The lord nods once. You are trusted with more.
The lord is silent a long time, then pleased.

events.text: A warrant-bearer is asking every god at the Divine Exchange about a hand that matches yours.

choices.text: Stay out of the Exchange an age

ok.log: The bearer asks for an age and moves on.

fail.log: The bearer finds someone who remembers.

choices.text: Lend the bearer another hand to follow

effects.log: You give the bearer a better trail, someone else's.

events.text: The paper names {npc}, the miller. You watch a week and see {him} grind the poor's grain for nothing on the last day of each month.

effects.log: The Lodge does not pay for flour.
You tell the Lodge the mill was shut.
The coins came from the other miller. You go to the other mill.

events.text: {npc} is the ferrymaster, and the only one who will cross the flood when a child is sick on the far bank.

effects.log: Somebody else will learn to cross.
You let the ferry keep its master.
The one who paid owns the bridge upstream. You visit the bridge.

events.text: {npc} sings in the square on market days, and every song is about someone the reeve wronged.

effects.log: Songs are not your business.
You let {him} keep singing.
The one who paid is the reeve. You visit the reeve.

events.text: {npc} drinks from the well in {his} own yard, and nobody else draws from it.

choices.text: Go to the well at night

ok.log: {npc} drinks in the morning and goes back to bed.

fail.log: The yard dog wakes the house.

effects.log: You leave the yard.

events.text: {npc} buys a pie from the same baker every evening on the way home.

ok.log: The apprentice hands over a different pie.

fail.log: The apprentice runs to {npc} with your coins.

ok.log: Nobody notices the new baker for one evening.

fail.log: The baker comes back early.

choices.text: Walk past the bakery and go

effects.log: You walk past the bakery and out of town.

events.text: {npc} is laid up with gout and takes a tonic from the herb-wife each night.

ok.log: The gout troubles {npc} no more.

fail.log: The herb-wife smells the bottle.

effects.log: You let the herb-wife do the work.

events.text: {npc} rides to the hunt every autumn through the beech wood, and the riders spread out among the trees.

ok.log: A riderless horse comes out of the wood.

fail.log: The hounds find you first.

effects.log: You watch the hunt ride by.

events.text: {npc} crosses the frozen lake on foot every winter to the fair on the far shore.

ok.log: The ice keeps it.

fail.log: {npc} is surer on the ice than you.

effects.log: You let {him} cross.

events.text: {npc} rides home late from the tavern every market day, alone, by the hollow road.

ok.log: The horse finds its own way home.

fail.log: Two friends ride behind {npc} tonight.

effects.log: You let {him} go.

events.text: A season as {npc}'s groom. Tonight {he} comes to the stable alone to see a mare foal.

ok.log: {npc} sits down in the straw and does not get up.

fail.log: The stable boy comes in with a lamp.

choices.text: Help with the foal, and go

effects.log: The foal is born. In the morning the groom is gone.

events.text: All summer you have kept {npc}'s accounts. Tonight {he} stays late to count the money with you.

ok.log: The count stops.

fail.log: {npc} looks up from the coins.

effects.log: The accounts balance. The clerk does not come back.

events.text: You have read to {npc}'s old mother every evening for a month. Tonight {npc} sits in to listen.

ok.log: The old woman sleeps. So does {npc}, for good.

fail.log: The old woman is awake after all.

effects.log: The reader does not come back.

events.text: {npc} meets you at the crossroads gallows-tree at midnight, as the old custom of this world allows.

ok.log: The crossroads keeps one more story.

fail.log: {npc} walks home. You crawl.
fail.deathCause: a crossroads duel for the Lodge

effects.log: You bow and take the other road.

events.text: {npc} has heard about the paper and waits for you on the bridge with a quarterstaff.

ok.log: The river takes the quarterstaff.

fail.log: The quarterstaff wins.
fail.deathCause: a bridge duel for the Lodge

effects.log: You do not cross.

events.text: {npc} invites you into {his} yard, shuts the gate, and draws an old soldier's sword.

ok.log: The yard is quiet.

fail.log: {npc} opens the gate for you to limp out.
fail.deathCause: a yard duel for the Lodge

effects.log: You ask {him} to open the gate. {He} does.

events.text: {npc} keeps a hired wrestler at the door, a giant who eats at the door and sleeps standing.

ok.log: The wrestler sits down, dazed. The door opens.

fail.log: The wrestler throws you into the street.
fail.deathCause: a hired wrestler

ok.log: The cellar door was never locked.

fail.log: The cellar door was.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: {npc}'s three sons take turns at the gate with cudgels.

ok.log: The eldest son sleeps by the gate. The house is open.

fail.log: The sons drive you off.
fail.deathCause: a son at the gate

choices.text: Wait for the change at the gate

ok.log: Between sons, you are through.

fail.log: They change early.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: A geese-yard lies between the wall and {npc}'s window, and geese wake for anything.

ok.log: Not one goose stirs.

fail.log: Every goose wakes.

ok.log: The geese are busy. You are not.

fail.log: The geese want more bread.

effects.log: You leave.

events.text: {npc}, grown, is the new smith in your town. {He} has been making one blade all month, and you know whose eyes those are.

ok.log: The forge goes cold.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you remember being at that age.

ok.log: You leave {him} at the forge, beaten.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay down.

ok.log: You tell {him} who paid. The new blade goes another way.

fail.log: {npc} will not hear a word of it.

effects.log: You leave town.

events.text: {npc} has followed you from village to village with a list of names, and yours is the last.

ok.log: The list is finished.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you remember being at that age.

ok.log: You tear the list and leave {him} on the road.

fail.log: {npc} does not stay down.

ok.log: You read the list with {him}. Most of the names paid the Lodge.

fail.log: {npc} will not hear a word of it.

effects.log: You walk on. {npc} follows.

events.text: The master of the Lampless Lodge asks you to choose the next paper yourself, from the whole box.

effects.log: The master nods. You are trusted with more.
The master laughs quietly and takes it back.

events.text: A hunter of the kingdom's warrants is showing your likeness at every inn on the high road.

ok.log: The hunter gives up and goes home.

fail.log: The hunter is patient.

choices.text: Pay a lookalike to be seen elsewhere

effects.log: Your lookalike is seen in three towns at once.
